top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, B048) credits an identifiable originating model of selection into exporting and reallocation across firms. Its qualitative predictions (exporter premia, selection, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data across many countries for over twenty years. The credit divides cleanly between two names, and a citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism avoids claiming priority over the empirical firm-level foundations (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum). Residual risks are that priority question and the dependence of welfare-gain magnitudes on functional form. These do not make the achievement unworthy of an award, so I rank it above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my documented co-authors and networks (Uppsala/IFAU labour economists, Oosterbeek, van Ours) do not include Melitz or Helpman. As a labour economist who values credible identification, I may favour candidates with tested predictions. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
